content.tex: Section A
Investigation Factors and multiples
You are advised to spend no more than 45 minutes on this section.
In this investigation you will look at the connection between factors and multiples of numbers.
A factor of a number divides into the number without leaving a remainder. A multiple of a number is in that number’s times table.
Examples
Factors of 10 are \(1, 2, 5\) and \(10\quad 10 \div 1 = 10\) remainder \(0\quad 10 \div 2 = 5\) remainder 0 \(10 \div 5 = 2\) remainder \(0\quad 10 \div 10 = 1\) remainder 0
Any other number leaves a remainder \(10 \div 3 = 3\) remainder 1 so 3 is not a factor of 10
Multiples of 7 are \(7, 14, 21, 28\) and so on
\(7 \times 1 = 7\quad 7 \times 2 = 14\quad 7 \times 3 = 21\quad 7 \times 4 = 28\)

parts.text: (b) The highest number that is both a factor of 4 and a factor of 10 is called the highest common factor (HCF) of 4 and 10.
